pr_title: Fixing the 'chunks' pointer so that it is not used before modifying a…
pr_body:
…gainst nullptr.

Adding a nullptr check before the pointer is used in the if-statement and before any memory is freed. Addressing issue #65604 where  the 'chunks' pointer was utilized before it was verified against nullptr.

fixes #65604

issue_context.title: The 'chunks' pointer was utilized before it was verified against nullptr. Check lines: 354, 366. rid_owner.h 354
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

8899f1eec213620c421ba16c07cf1b3681c5a25d

### System information

Windows 11, GLES3, RTX 3000

### Issue description

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8f05263bd5417f1afeb46405a53a49c687b39240/core/templates/rid_owner.h#L354-L371

> V595 The 'chunks' pointer was utilized before it was verified against nullptr. Check lines: 354, 366. rid_owner.h 354

### Steps to reproduce

Use pvsstudio in trace mode to compile godot on MSVC Windows.

### Minimal reproduction project

This is using the Godot Engine as the static analysis target.
comments:
I will take care of this issue. Please assign me to it. 

Thank you.
For potential contributors: see discussion in #66787 for additional context.

review_comments: This should not be necessary, `chunks` is `null` only if `max_alloc == 0` (in this case, for loop will be skipped) or `memrealloc` failed (in this case, it will crash in `_allocate_rid()`).

The checker doesn't recognize this implication, hence the issue, not sure where it would be best to put the check, along with the max alloc?

On second thought maybe the error shows up because the actual null check below is unnecessary?

In this case, PVS-Studio probably want's us to check return value of `memrealloc` on the line `94`, and do something if it's `nullptr`. This is technically valid, but in practice if we failed to allocate 64 bytes it's not much we can do, except `CRASH_COND_MSG(!chunks, "Out of memory");`.

> On second thought maybe the error shows up because the actual null check below is unnecessary?

No, this check is valid, this code is reachable if no RIDs were allocated.
Oh yes my bad, misread the indentation and thought the freeing was inside the check
